column1: # The mammalian lipid reaction network of BioPAN (LIPID MAPS; Gaud et al., F1000Research 2021),
# transcribed from the tool's own database (biopan_reaction and biopan_reaction_gene in the archived
# source, https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/PKD6B, GPL-3): 51 reactions between lipid classes, 13 over
# the ether lipids, 3 over the dihydro sphingoid bases and 30 between fatty acids, with the genes
# BioPAN names for each. Every gene is the human symbol: BioPAN's database gives the two
# stearoyl-CoA desaturases as the mouse Scd1 and Scd3, which are SCD and SCD5 here (human has those
# two; Scd3 has no one-to-one orthologue). Below them, marked "extension", the steps MIL-X adds
# for classes a lipidomics run confirms and BioPAN does not cover: the glycosphingolipids, the
# kind says how a reaction maps molecular species onto one another:
#   preserving  the chains are kept; PE 34:1 -> PC 34:1
#   removes     one chain is lost; PC 16:0_18:1 -> LPC 16:0 or LPC 18:1 (needs the chains resolved)
#   adds        one chain is gained; LPC 16:0 -> PC 16:0_18:1 (needs the product's chains resolved)
#   class       only the whole classes relate; Chol -> CE
#   fa          a fatty-acid step, between chains summed over the species that carry them
